EM.name: Engineering Mathematics

high_yield_formulas.name: Trace & Determinant with Eigenvalues
high_yield_formulas.notes: Use this first to eliminate 3 out of 4 MCQ options in 15 seconds.

high_yield_formulas.name: Euler's Planar Graph Formula
high_yield_formulas.formula: V - E + R = 2 (for connected planar graphs)
high_yield_formulas.notes: E <= 3V - 6 for simple graphs (V >= 3). E <= 2V - 4 if no triangles.

high_yield_formulas.name: Handshaking Lemma
high_yield_formulas.notes: Number of odd-degree vertices is always EVEN.

high_yield_formulas.name: Bayes' Theorem
high_yield_formulas.notes: P(B) is total probability: ∑ P(B|A_i) P(A_i).

key_theorems.title: Cayley-Hamilton Theorem
key_theorems.statement: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation: det(A - λI) = 0.

key_theorems.title: Lagrange's Theorem
key_theorems.statement: The order of any subgroup H divides the order of finite group G.

key_theorems.title: Rolle's & Mean Value Theorem
key_theorems.statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), then f'(c) = [f(b) - f(a)] / (b - a).

exam_traps: Vacuous Truth: If hypothesis P is False, implication P -> Q is ALWAYS True!
In disconnected planar graphs with k components, Euler formula is V - E + R = 1 + k.
Poisson distribution has mean EQUAL to variance: Mean = Var = λ.

DL.name: Digital Logic

high_yield_formulas.name: 2's Complement Range (n-bit)
high_yield_formulas.notes: For 8 bits: -128 to +127.

high_yield_formulas.name: Consensus Theorem
high_yield_formulas.notes: BC is redundant consensus term.

high_yield_formulas.name: Mod-N Counter Sizing
high_yield_formulas.notes: Ring counter has n states; Johnson counter has 2n states.

high_yield_formulas.name: Adder Overflow Detector
high_yield_formulas.formula: V = C_{in} ⊕ C_{out} (of MSB sign bit)
high_yield_formulas.notes: V = 1 indicates arithmetic overflow.

key_theorems.title: De Morgan's Dual Laws
key_theorems.statement: (A + B)' = A' B' and (A B)' = A' + B'.

key_theorems.title: JK Characteristic Equation
key_theorems.statement: Q_next = J Q' + K' Q.

key_theorems.title: T Flip-Flop Equation
key_theorems.statement: Q_next = T ⊕ Q.

exam_traps: Race-around condition occurs when J=1, K=1 and clock width t_w > flip-flop delay t_pd.
Active-LOW enable inputs: decoder only functions when enable pin is 0.
IEEE-754 exponent 0 and 255 are reserved for special representations (0/denorm and Inf/NaN).

COA.name: Computer Organization & Architecture

high_yield_formulas.name: Average Memory Access Time (AMAT)
high_yield_formulas.notes: Multi-level: t_L1 + m_L1 * (t_L2 + m_L2 * t_mem).

high_yield_formulas.name: Pipeline Speedup
high_yield_formulas.formula: S = (n * k) / (k + n - 1)  |  Ideal Speedup = k (number of stages)
high_yield_formulas.notes: Clock cycle time = max(stage delays) + latch delay.

high_yield_formulas.name: Effective CPI with Stalls
high_yield_formulas.notes: Branch penalty = branch frequency * branch stall cycles.

high_yield_formulas.name: Set-Associative Tag Bits
high_yield_formulas.formula: Tag bits = Total Address bits - Set bits - Offset bits
high_yield_formulas.notes: Set bits = log2(Cache Size / (Associativity * Block Size)).

key_theorems.title: Principle of Locality
key_theorems.statement: Temporal locality (recently accessed data) and Spatial locality (nearby memory locations).

key_theorems.title: Amdahl's Law
key_theorems.statement: Speedup = 1 / [ (1 - f) + f / s ] where f is enhanced fraction.

exam_traps: In PC-Relative addressing, remember PC has ALREADY advanced to the next instruction!
Write-Through ensures memory is always consistent; Write-Back uses dirty bit to defer writes.
Hardwired control units are strictly FASTER than microprogrammed control units.

PDS.name: Programming and Data Structures

high_yield_formulas.name: Unique BST Count (Catalan)
high_yield_formulas.notes: Number of structurally distinct BSTs with n distinct keys.

high_yield_formulas.name: Complete Binary Tree Leaves
high_yield_formulas.notes: In a strict binary tree: Leaves L = Internal nodes I + 1.

high_yield_formulas.name: AVL Tree Minimum Nodes
high_yield_formulas.notes: Fibonacci recurrence for height-balanced trees.

key_theorems.title: BST Inorder Property
key_theorems.statement: The Inorder traversal of any BST is strictly sorted in ascending order.

key_theorems.title: Linear Heap Construction
key_theorems.statement: Bottom-up Build-Heap builds a heap from n elements in strictly O(n) linear time.

exam_traps: Circular queue of capacity N stores at most N - 1 elements to avoid full/empty ambiguity.
*(p + i) is identical to p[i] and i[p] in standard C pointer arithmetic.
Static local variables in C persist across function invocations in the data segment.

ALGO.name: Algorithms

high_yield_formulas.name: Master Theorem
high_yield_formulas.formula: T(n) = a T(n/b) + Θ(n^k log^p n)
high_yield_formulas.notes: Compare a with b^k. If a > b^k => Θ(n^(log_b a)).

high_yield_formulas.name: Comparison Sort Lower Bound
high_yield_formulas.notes: Derived from binary decision tree of height log2(n!).

high_yield_formulas.name: Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs
high_yield_formulas.notes: Time complexity Θ(V³) using dynamic programming.

key_theorems.title: MST Cut Property
key_theorems.statement: The minimum weight edge crossing any cut in a connected graph must belong to every MST.

key_theorems.title: Dijkstra Non-Negativity
key_theorems.statement: Dijkstra's greedy choice property requires non-negative edge weights to guarantee correctness.

exam_traps: Dijkstra algorithm fails with negative edge weights; use Bellman-Ford (O(V*E)) instead.
Quick Sort worst case is O(n²) when the chosen pivot is always the smallest or largest element.
0/1 Knapsack cannot be solved by greedy method; requires Dynamic Programming.

TOC.name: Theory of Computation

high_yield_formulas.name: NFA to DFA State Bound
high_yield_formulas.notes: Powerset construction upper bound.

high_yield_formulas.name: CNF Derivation Length
high_yield_formulas.formula: Steps = 2n - 1 for string of length n
high_yield_formulas.notes: Chomsky Normal Form productions A -> BC or A -> a.

key_theorems.title: Myhill-Nerode Theorem
key_theorems.statement: The number of states in a minimal DFA equals the number of equivalence classes of R_L.

key_theorems.title: Rice's Theorem
key_theorems.statement: Any non-trivial semantic property of the language of a Turing Machine is undecidable.

key_theorems.title: Halting Problem
key_theorems.statement: Determining whether an arbitrary Turing Machine halts on an arbitrary input is undecidable.

exam_traps: CFLs are NOT closed under intersection or complementation, but ARE closed under intersection with regular languages.
Deterministic Context-Free Languages (DCFLs) ARE closed under complementation.
Ambiguity of a Context-Free Grammar is undecidable.

CD.name: Compiler Design

high_yield_formulas.name: Parser Power Hierarchy
high_yield_formulas.notes: Number of states: LR(0) == SLR(1) == LALR(1) < CLR(1).

high_yield_formulas.name: LL(1) Conflict-Free Test
high_yield_formulas.formula: FIRST(α) ∩ FIRST(β) = ∅ and (if ε ∈ α) FIRST(β) ∩ FOLLOW(A) = ∅
high_yield_formulas.notes: Left recursion or common prefixes immediately violate LL(1).

key_theorems.title: LALR State Merging Invariance
key_theorems.statement: Merging core states in CLR(1) to form LALR(1) can never create Shift-Reduce conflicts.

key_theorems.title: S-Attributed SDD Evaluation
key_theorems.statement: S-attributed definitions use only synthesized attributes and can be evaluated bottom-up.

exam_traps: An ambiguous grammar can NEVER be parsed by any deterministic parser (neither LL nor LR).
Liveness analysis is a backward data flow analysis problem.
Constant folding is compile-time evaluation (2 * 3 -> 6); Constant propagation replaces variables with known constants.

OS.name: Operating Systems

high_yield_formulas.name: Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT)
high_yield_formulas.notes: Multi-level paging adds t_mem for each additional level on TLB miss.

high_yield_formulas.name: Deadlock-Free Resource Condition
high_yield_formulas.notes: n processes each needing at most m instances of a single resource.

high_yield_formulas.name: Disk SCAN Head Movement
high_yield_formulas.notes: Assuming head moves toward larger cylinders first.

key_theorems.title: Coffman Deadlock Conditions
key_theorems.statement: Deadlock requires Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.

key_theorems.title: Belady's Anomaly
key_theorems.statement: FIFO page replacement can exhibit more page faults when allocated more physical frames.

exam_traps: Peterson's algorithm is formulated specifically for 2 processes, not arbitrary n processes.
Fork() returns 0 to the child and child's PID to parent. Total processes after k forks = 2^k.
In inverted page tables, table size is proportional to physical RAM frames, not virtual space.

DB.name: Databases

high_yield_formulas.name: Normal Form Determinants
high_yield_formulas.formula: BCNF: X -> Y requires X is Superkey. 3NF: X is Superkey OR Y is Prime.
high_yield_formulas.notes: If all attributes are prime, the relation is automatically in 3NF.

high_yield_formulas.name: B+ Tree Node Capacities
high_yield_formulas.formula: Max keys = p - 1  |  Min internal keys = ⌈p / 2⌉ - 1
high_yield_formulas.notes: Order p = maximum child tree pointers per node.

key_theorems.title: Conflict Serializability Theorem
key_theorems.statement: A schedule S is conflict serializable if and only if its precedence graph has NO directed cycles.

key_theorems.title: Strict 2PL Recovery Guarantee
key_theorems.statement: Strict 2PL prevents cascading aborts and guarantees conflict serializability.

exam_traps: In SQL, NULL compared with any value evaluates to UNKNOWN. COUNT(col) ignores NULLs; COUNT(*) includes them.
Weak entity primary key must include the partial discriminator PLUS the identifying strong entity primary key.
View serializability is NP-complete to test; Conflict serializability is O(V + E) using cycle detection.

CN.name: Computer Networks

high_yield_formulas.name: Stop-and-Wait Efficiency
high_yield_formulas.notes: Throughput = η * Bandwidth.

high_yield_formulas.name: CSMA/CD Minimum Frame Size
high_yield_formulas.notes: Ensures sender is still transmitting when a collision reflection arrives.

high_yield_formulas.name: Sliding Window Maximum Sizing
high_yield_formulas.formula: Go-Back-N: W_s = 2^k - 1  |  Selective Repeat: W_s = W_r = 2^(k-1)
high_yield_formulas.notes: Prevents sequence number ambiguity on wrap-around.

high_yield_formulas.name: IPv4 Fragment Offset
high_yield_formulas.notes: Measured in 8-byte units in the IPv4 packet header.

key_theorems.title: Longest Prefix Match
key_theorems.statement: CIDR forwarding routes to the routing table entry with the longest subnet mask prefix.

key_theorems.title: TCP Congestion Additive Increase
key_theorems.statement: In Congestion Avoidance, cwnd increases by 1 MSS per successful Round Trip Time (RTT).

exam_traps: TCP SYN, FIN, and RST packets consume 1 sequence number even if they carry 0 application payload bytes.
In Go-Back-N, receiver window is ALWAYS 1; in Selective Repeat, sender and receiver windows are equal.
Subnet usable hosts = 2^(host_bits) - 2 (subtract all-0s network ID and all-1s broadcast address).

GA.name: General Aptitude

high_yield_formulas.name: Relative Speed Formula
high_yield_formulas.formula: Opposite: S1 + S2  |  Same direction: |S1 - S2|
high_yield_formulas.notes: Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18.

high_yield_formulas.name: Work and Time
high_yield_formulas.notes: Pipes: inlet pipe has positive rate; leak/emptying pipe has negative rate.

high_yield_formulas.name: Circular Permutation
high_yield_formulas.notes: For necklaces or garlands where clockwise == anticlockwise: (n - 1)! / 2.

key_theorems.title: Subject-Verb Proximity Rule
key_theorems.statement: In 'either... or' and 'neither... nor', verb agrees in number with the closest subject.

key_theorems.title: Cube Opposite Faces Rule
key_theorems.statement: On a standard die or unfolded cube, opposite faces never share a common vertex or edge.

exam_traps: Always check units: km/h vs m/s and hours vs minutes before calculating answers.
General Aptitude carries 15 marks with high scoring potential; spend the first 25 minutes of the exam here.
Watch out for absolute words in verbal comprehension: 'all', 'never', 'must' are rarely supported by neutral passages.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Which of the following propositions is a CONTRADICTION?
practiceQuestions.explanation: P ^ ~P is always False regardless of the truth value of P.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Let A and B be sets such that |A| = 4 and |B| = 3. What is the total number of functions from A to B?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Number of functions from set A to set B is |B|^|A| = 3^4 = 81.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: What is the rank of a 4x4 matrix whose all entries are equal to 1?
practiceQuestions.explanation: All rows are identical. Row reduction reduces it to 1 non-zero row. Rank = 1.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: If a 3x3 real symmetric matrix has eigenvalues 0, 2, and 4, which of the following is TRUE?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Since one eigenvalue is 0, Det(A) = 0 * 2 * 4 = 0, so A is non-invertible/singular.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: In how many ways can 5 boys and 5 girls sit in a circle such that no two girls sit together?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Seat 5 boys in a circle in (5 - 1)! = 4! = 24 ways. This creates 5 gaps. Seat 5 girls in these 5 gaps in 5! = 120 ways. Total = 24 * 120 = 2880.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Evaluate: lim (x -> 0) [ (1 - cos(2x)) / x^2 ].

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Let X be a continuous uniform random variable in [0, 10]. Find P(2 <= X <= 7).

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: A relation R on a set A is a PARTIAL ORDER if it is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: A partial order is defined as reflexive, anti-symmetric, and transitive.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: What is the chromatic number of any complete bipartite graph K_{m, n} with m, n >= 1?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Any bipartite graph can have its vertices 2-colored (one color for each partition set). Chromatic number = 2.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: If A is an orthogonal matrix (A^T * A = I), what are the possible values of det(A)?
practiceQuestions.explanation: det(A^T A) = det(A)^2 = det(I) = 1 => det(A) = ±1.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Which of the following matrices is/are DIAGONALIZABLE?

options.A: Any n x n matrix with n distinct eigenvalues

practiceQuestions.explanation: Matrices with distinct eigenvalues, symmetric matrices, and identity matrices are diagonalizable. Non-zero nilpotent matrices are never diagonalizable.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Which of the following graphs is/are BIPARTITE?

options.B: Any cycle with an EVEN number of vertices

practiceQuestions.explanation: A graph is bipartite iff it has no odd cycles. Trees, even cycles, and K_2 have no odd cycles. K_3 is an odd cycle (triangle).

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Which of the following propositions is/are TAUTOLOGIES?
practiceQuestions.explanation: All 4 propositions evaluate to True under all truth value assignments.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: For any two events A and B with P(B) > 0, which of the following is/are ALWAYS TRUE?

options.B: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
options.C: If A and B are independent, P(A|B) = P(A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: All 4 statements are foundational probability identities.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Which of the following algebraic structures is/are GROUPS?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Z under multiplication is not a group because integers other than ±1 lack multiplicative inverses.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: The number of edges in a complete graph with 8 vertices (K_8) is _________.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: Let A be a 2x2 matrix with Trace = 5 and Det = 6. The largest eigenvalue of A is _________.
practiceQuestions.explanation: λ^2 - 5λ + 6 = 0 => (λ - 2)(λ - 3) = 0. Largest eigenvalue is 3.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: The coefficient of x^3 in the polynomial expansion of (1 + 2x)^5 is _________.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: If random variable X has Poisson distribution with mean 4, the variance of X is _________.
practiceQuestions.explanation: In a Poisson distribution, Mean == Variance = λ = 4.

practiceQuestions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
practiceQuestions.text: How many reflexive relations can be defined on a set with 4 elements?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Formula for reflexive relations is 2^(n^2 - n). For n = 4: 2^(16 - 4) = 2^12 = 4096.
